titleEn: Exclusive: Plantik and Hudson River Biotechnology team up to de-risk heat-tolerant strawberries
titleZh: Plantik与Hudson River Biotechnology联手开发耐热草莓
summaryZh: Plantik Biosciences与Hudson River Biotechnology达成合作，将Plantik在番茄中验证的耐热靶点与Hudson River的无转基因草莓基因组编辑技术相结合，开发可授权的耐热草莓性状。该合作旨在降低育种门槛，让中小型育种者也能获得原本仅大型种子公司才具备的基因编辑能力，验证试验已在进行中。
featuredReason: 该合作展示了AI驱动的"暗基因组"编辑技术在作物耐热育种中的商业化路径，以及平台化模式如何降低中小育种者的技术门槛。对于关注智慧农业中AI+基因编辑交叉创新、以及气候变化应对方案的从业者具有参考价值。
contentFull:
[Disclosure: AgFunderNews’ parent company AgFunder is an investor in Plantik.]

Plantik Biosciences and Hudson River Biotechnology are partnering to develop heat tolerance in crops, with the goal of producing a validated heat-tolerance trait any strawberry breeder can license.

By combining heat-tolerant targets identified and validated by Plantik in tomatoes with “transgene-free” strawberry genome editing methods developed by Hudson River, the companies hope to turn trait discoveries into “improved strawberry varieties.” Validation trials are already underway.

According to Plantik cofounder and CEO Ying Shao, heat tolerance is “a must-have trait for many crops across the globe” thanks to the rise in extreme heat events worldwide in recent years. Strawberries are among the most exposed crops, as these high temperatures disrupt flowering and fruit set, and damage overall fruit quality.

Performance under high heat

France-based Plantik employs its ATLANTIS machine learning platform to search “the dark genome,” the regulatory stretches of DNA in plants that switch genes on and off. It then edits those regions without inserting any foreign DNA, allowing plant breeders to fast-track development of crops.

Plantik’s first product is a heat-tolerant tomato, which the company claims it developed in about 12 months instead of the five to eight years required by traditional breeding.

The company is currently running demonstrations across greenhouses and fields in the US and Belgium.

“We have now worked on this trait in multiple tomato crops, from lab tomatoes to now commercial hybrids,” says Shao. “Overall, we see that in the real conditions, the material also performs much better in terms of yield preservation under high heat.”

Trials from summer 2026 for genome-edited high-heat-tolerant tomato varieties. Image credit: Plantik Biosciences.
Editing at speed

Hudson River says its BioMaas platform gives breeders access to genome editing without the time and expense of building the R&D in-house. Thus far the company has focused on tomatoes and strawberries.

“We have now developed technical capabilities that allow us to very rapidly deploy new traits in those crops, like the heat-tolerant trait,” says Hudson River CEO Fernando Los. He adds that the company can now make complex edits in these crops “in a matter of months.” Changes to EU rules, which simplify CRISPR regulations, have also caused “a surge of interest” in the business.

Los says the open nature of the Hudson River platform is the company’s biggest differentiator. Breeders get the technology plus a range of traits, including new proprietary traits like heat tolerance. Third-party trait developers such as Plantik get access to Hudson River’s network of breeders.

In this specific partnership, BioMass will act “as a bridge” between trait innovators like Plantik and breeders. Beginning with strawberries, Plantik will identify which parts of the genome to edit for heat tolerance, and Hudson River makes those edits in the plants.

“Strawberry is a different story from tomato because it’s genetically much more complex,” says Los. “It’s an octoploid species rather than a diploid. Propagation is normally done clonaly, so you cannot create seeds; you have to work directly in relevant commercial germplasm, which are all things that we can do.”

Strawberry is the starting point, and the companies plan to take the approach to other crops later. They are also inviting other companies to bring trait challenges for their own strawberry varieties.

De-risking heat tolerance for breeders

The technical, regulatory, and financial demands of trait discovery and gene editing mean breeders outside of the largest seed companies are unlikely to accomplish this process alone in the same timeframe, says Los.

“Even [the largest] companies have limited team capacity, limited budget.”

Strawberry breeders have it hardest, he adds, because they lack the resources to run a full genome editing workflow in-house.

“What we offer here is essentially de-risking and very cheap access to a piece of technology that’s normally only available to the very largest companies,” says Los. “If you reduce the failure rate from 90% to maybe 10% for a breeder, that’s a very good proposition to offer them.”

translationZh:
[披露：AgFunderNews的母公司AgFunder是Plantik的投资者。]

Plantik Biosciences与Hudson River Biotechnology正在合作开发作物的耐热性，目标是产生一个经过验证的耐热性状，任何草莓育种者都可以授权使用。

通过将Plantik在番茄中识别和验证的耐热靶点与Hudson River开发的"无转基因"草莓基因组编辑方法相结合，两家公司希望将性状发现转化为"改良的草莓品种"。验证试验已经在进行中。

据Plantik联合创始人兼首席执行官Ying Shao表示，由于近年来全球极端高温事件增多，耐热性已成为"全球许多作物的必备性状"。草莓是最容易受到影响的作物之一，因为高温会扰乱开花和坐果，并损害果实的整体品质。

**高温下的表现**

总部位于法国的Plantik利用其ATLANTIS机器学习平台搜索"暗基因组"，即植物中控制基因开关的调控性DNA区域。然后它编辑这些区域而不插入任何外源DNA，使植物育种者能够加速作物开发。

Plantik的第一个产品是耐热番茄，该公司声称在大约12个月内完成了开发，而传统育种需要五到八年。

该公司目前正在美国和比利时的温室和田间进行示范。

"我们现在已经在多个番茄作物中研究了这个性状，从实验室番茄到现在的商业杂交品种，"Shao说。"总体而言，我们在真实条件下看到，该材料在高温下的产量保持方面也表现得好得多。"

**快速编辑**

Hudson River表示，其BioMaas平台让育种者无需投入时间和费用自建研发团队即可获得基因组编辑能力。迄今为止，该公司专注于番茄和草莓。

"我们现在已经开发出技术能力，使我们能够非常快速地在这些作物中部署新性状，比如耐热性状，"Hudson River首席执行官Fernando Los说。他补充说，公司现在可以在这些作物中"在几个月内"完成复杂的编辑。欧盟规则的改变简化了CRISPR监管，也引发了"业务的激增"。

Los表示，Hudson River平台的开放性是该公司的最大差异化优势。育种者获得技术以及一系列性状，包括耐热性等新的专有性状。像Plantik这样的第三方性状开发者也获得了Hudson River育种者网络的访问权限。

在这个特定的合作中，BioMaas将充当像Plantik这样的性状创新者与育种者之间的"桥梁"。从草莓开始，Plantik将确定基因组中哪些部分需要编辑以实现耐热性，Hudson River则在植物中进行这些编辑。

"草莓与番茄不同，因为它在遗传上要复杂得多，"Los说。"它是一个八倍体物种而非二倍体。繁殖通常通过克隆进行，所以你不能产生种子；你必须直接在相关的商业种质中工作，而这些都是我们能做的。"

草莓是起点，两家公司计划稍后将这种方法扩展到其他作物。他们还邀请其他公司为其自己的草莓品种带来性状挑战。

**为育种者降低耐热性风险**

Los表示，性状发现和基因编辑的技术、监管和财务要求意味着，大型种子公司以外的育种者不太可能在相同的时间框架内独自完成这一过程。

"即使是[最大的]公司，团队能力和预算也有限。"

他补充说，草莓育种者面临的困难最大，因为他们缺乏资源在内部运行完整的基因组编辑工作流程。

"我们在这里提供的基本上是降低风险和以非常低的成本获取通常只有最大型公司才能获得的技术，"Los说。"如果你能将育种者的失败率从90%降低到也许10%，那对他们来说是一个非常不错的提议。"
author: Jennifer Marston
